title: Labyrinths of Time
subtitle: Contributed by patron Elena Rostova
author: Jorge Luis Borges
synopsis: An exploration of timeless labyrinths and recursive philosophical puzzles.

title: The Shadow of the Wind
subtitle: The Cemetery of Forgotten Books, Volume I
author: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
synopsis: Hidden in the heart of the old city of Barcelona is the 'Cemetery of Forgotten Books', a labyrinthine library of obscure and abandoned titles in the care of the antiquarian book trade. To this secret precinct, ten-year-old Daniel Sempere is conducted by his bookseller father in the summer of 1945.
synopsisExtended: Daniel is allowed to choose one book from the shelves and pulls out La Sombra del Viento by Julián Carax. But as Daniel grows, his efforts to discover the author's destiny reveal that someone has been systematically hunting down and burning every last copy of Carax's published works. What begins as a boy’s infatuation turns into an epic descent into a labyrinth of murder, madness, and doomed love across Spain’s darkest decades.
quote: Every book, every volume you see here, has a soul. The soul of the person who wrote it and of those who read it and lived and dreamed with it.
chapter: Chapter IV: The Cemetery of Forgotten Books

title: Invisible Cities
subtitle: Cities & Memory, Reflections on Empire
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: Marco Polo describes to Kublai Khan the cities that cannot exist on normal charts, constructed from memory, desire, signs, and regret in poetic dialogues.
synopsisExtended: In a garden in the evening, the aging Emperor Kublai Khan listens as Venetian traveler Marco Polo describes cities in the distant corners of his vast empire—cities built of spiderwebs, cities on stilts over water, cities of mirrors, and cities where the dead duplicate the lives of the living.
quote: Memory's images, once they are fixed in words, are erased. Perhaps I am afraid of losing Venice all at once, if I speak of it.

title: Piranesi
subtitle: The Beauty of the House is Immeasurable
author: Susanna Clarke
synopsis: Piranesi’s house is no ordinary building: its rooms are infinite, its corridors endless, its walls lined with thousands upon thousands of statues.
synopsisExtended: Within the labyrinth of halls an ocean is imprisoned; waves rush up staircases, rooms are flooded in an instant. But Piranesi is not afraid. He lives to explore the House, aided by his journals and his companion, The Other, until evidence of a sixteenth person appears.
quote: The Beauty of the House is immeasurable; its Kindness infinite.

title: Klara and the Sun
subtitle: A Novel of Devotion and Perception
author: Kazuo Ishiguro
synopsis: An Artificial Friend with outstanding observational qualities watches the behavior of those who come into her store from her place on the shelf.
synopsisExtended: Klara remains hopeful that a customer will soon choose her, but when the possibility emerges that her circumstances may change forever, she is warned not to invest too much in the promises of humans.
quote: Do you believe in the human heart? I don't mean simply the organ, obviously. But do you believe there's something that makes each of us special and individual?

title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
subtitle: The Chronicle of Macondo
author: Gabriel García Márquez
synopsis: The brilliant chronicle of the rise and fall of the mythical town of Macondo through seven generations of the Buendía family.
synopsisExtended: Blending myth, comedy, tragedy, and political reality, Márquez's epic captures the cyclical sweep of history, human ambition, alchemy, and loneliness.
quote: Many years later, as he faced the firing squad, Colonel Aureliano Buendía was to remember that distant afternoon when his father took him to discover ice.
chapter: Chapter I: The Discovery of Ice

title: The Overstory
subtitle: An Epic of Resistance and Arboreal Time
author: Richard Powers
synopsis: A sweeping, impassioned work of activism and resistance that is also a stunning evocation of the natural world.
synopsisExtended: Nine Americans whose unique life experiences with trees bring them together to address the destruction of forests, moving in ring structures like wood from roots to crown.
quote: You and the tree in your backyard came from a common ancestor. A billion and a half years ago, the two of you parted ways.

title: When Breath Becomes Air
subtitle: What Makes a Life Worth Living in the Face of Death
author: Paul Kalanithi
synopsis: A profoundly moving reflection on confronting mortality and what makes a life worth living in the face of death.
synopsisExtended: At thirty-six, on the verge of completing a decade's training as a neurosurgeon, Paul Kalanithi was diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. One day he was a doctor making a living treating the dying, and the next he was a patient struggling to live.
quote: You can't ever reach perfection, but you can believe in an asymptote toward which you are ceaselessly striving.

title: Drive Your Plow Over the Bones of the Dead
subtitle: An Existential Mystery of the Polish Woods
author: Olga Tokarczuk
synopsis: A subversive, entertaining noir novel that is an existential thriller about human madness and animal retribution.
synopsisExtended: In a remote Polish village, eccentric recluse Janina Duszejko translates William Blake, studies astrology, and watches over summer villas. When local hunters turn up dead under mysterious circumstances, Janina involves herself in the investigation.
quote: Its form is our prison, and inside we pace up and down, looking for doors.

title: The Library of Babel
subtitle: Hexagonal Galleries of the Universe
author: Jorge Luis Borges
synopsis: The universe (which others call the Library) is composed of an indefinite, perhaps infinite number of hexagonal galleries with vast air shafts between them.
synopsisExtended: Every book in this infinite library contains 410 pages of 40 lines each. Somewhere in its depths lies the catalog of catalogs, the vindications of all lives, and the true history of the universe.
quote: The universe (which others call the Library) is composed of an indefinite, perhaps infinite number of hexagonal galleries...
chapter: Folio I: The Architecture of Hexagons

title: Ficciones
subtitle: Tapestry of Mazes and Circular Ruins
author: Jorge Luis Borges
synopsis: A labyrinthine tapestry of philosophical conjectures, false encyclopedias, and circular ruins.
synopsisExtended: Contains 'Tlön, Uqbar, Orbis Tertius', 'The Garden of Forking Paths', 'Pierre Menard, Author of the Quixote', and 'The Circular Ruins'—stories that revolutionized 20th-century literature.
quote: Time forks perpetually towards innumerable futures. In one of them I am your enemy.
chapter: Part I: The Garden of Forking Paths

title: The Name of the Rose
subtitle: A Medieval Murder in an Alpine Abbey
author: Umberto Eco
synopsis: Stat rosa pristina nomine, nomina nuda tenemus. Murder and monastic heresy in a secluded alpine scriptorium.
synopsisExtended: The year is 1327. Franciscans in a wealthy Italian abbey are suspected of heresy, and Brother William of Baskerville arrives to investigate. When seven bizarre deaths take place in seven days, William must use the logic of Aristotle, the theology of Aquinas, and the empiricism of Roger Bacon.
quote: Books are not made to be believed, but to be subjected to inquiry. When we consider a book, we mustn't ask what it says but what it means.

title: If on a winter's night a traveler
subtitle: A Reader's Quest for the Lost Book
author: Italo Calvino
synopsis: You are about to begin reading Italo Calvino's new novel... Relax. Concentrate. Dispel every other thought.
synopsisExtended: The story of you, the Reader, trying to read a book called 'If on a winter's night a traveler' only to find the pages bound incorrectly, leading you into an international bibliophilic conspiracy and a search through ten unfinished masterpieces.
quote: You are about to begin reading Italo Calvino's new novel, If on a winter's night a traveler. Relax. Concentrate.
chapter: Chapter I: In the Railway Station

title: The Master and Margarita
subtitle: The Devil in Soviet Moscow
author: Mikhail Bulgakov
synopsis: Manuscripts don't burn. The devil visits Soviet Moscow with his retinue of mischievous spirits and a talking black cat.
synopsisExtended: A biting satirical comedy of communist Moscow paired with a heart-wrenching psychological reimagining of the trial of Jesus Christ under Pontius Pilate in ancient Jerusalem.
chapter: Chapter I: Never Talk with Strangers

title: Pedro Páramo
subtitle: A Descent into the Town of Whispers
author: Juan Rulfo
synopsis: I came to Comala because I was told that my father, a man named Pedro Páramo, was living there.
synopsisExtended: Juan Preciado promises his dying mother that he will return to her hometown of Comala to seek his father. He finds a ghostly, windswept town inhabited solely by the souls of the dead murmuring memories.
quote: This town is filled with echoes. It's like they were trapped in the hollows of the walls or under the stones.
chapter: Section I: Comala in the Heat

title: Solaris
subtitle: The Conscious Ocean of the Cosmos
author: Stanisław Lem
synopsis: We take off into the cosmos, ready for anything: for solitude, for hardship, for exhaustion, death. We are proud of ourselves...
synopsisExtended: Psychologist Kris Kelvin arrives on the research station orbiting the planet Solaris to study its vast living oceanic plasma, only to discover the researchers driven mad by physical manifestations from their deepest repressed memories.
quote: We have no need of other worlds. We need mirrors. We don't know what to do with other worlds.

title: The Book of Disquiet
subtitle: The Factless Autobiography of Bernardo Soares
author: Fernando Pessoa
synopsis: I'd rather read than live, although reading is also a form of living, perhaps the purest of all.
synopsisExtended: Written under the heteronym Bernardo Soares, an assistant bookkeeper in the city of Lisbon, this diary of contemplative fragments explores ennui, existence, dreams, and the poetry of everyday life.
quote: My soul is a hidden orchestra; I do not know which instruments strike and scrape inside me.
chapter: Fragment 1: In the Rua dos Douradores

title: The Complete Poems
subtitle: The Variorum Edition of Emily Dickinson
author: Emily Dickinson
synopsis: There is no Frigate like a Book / To take us Lands away / Nor any Coursers like a Page / Of prancing Poetry—
synopsisExtended: The complete, breathtaking poetic legacy of the Belle of Amherst, bound with her original idiosyncratic punctuation, botanical pressed flowers, and quiet metaphysical lightning.
quote: Hope is the thing with feathers that perches in the soul - and sings the tunes without the words - and never stops at all.

title: Labyrinths
subtitle: Selected Stories & Metaphysical Investigations
author: Jorge Luis Borges
translator: Donald A. Yates & James E. Irby
synopsis: Selected stories and other writings containing Borges' most celebrated metaphysical mysteries and paradoxes.
synopsisExtended: An essential compilation featuring twenty-three stories, ten parables, and eight essays that demonstrate Borges' singular visionary brilliance.
quote: A man sets out to draw the world. As the years go by, he peoples a space with images of provinces, kingdoms, mountains, bays... Shortly before he dies, he discovers that that patient labyrinth of lines traces the lineaments of his own face.
